text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- IOF INCREASE HARMLESS IN SHORT TERM

Last week's increase in the IOF financial transaction tax on credit operations, from six percent to 15 percent a year, will affect credit availability but a lot less than originally thought, according to banks and other credit providers.
-- DOLLARS EXCHANGED FOR REAIS TO BUY VALE

The Central Bank on Thursday bought $1.1 billion of a total $1.7 billion brought into the country by the CSN consortium to buy state mining firm CVRD. A judge last night overturned an injunction that had blocked the transfer of Vale shares to the new owners.
-- BRADESCO NET 201.9 MLN REAIS IN Q1
Brazil's and Latin America's largest retail bank Bradesco posted a 1997 first quarter profit of 201.9 million reais, a profit margin of 15.13 percent.
O GLOBO
-- PACT ENDS IMPASSE OVER CIVIL SERVICE REFORM

Opposition parties and the government reached an accord on several controversial issues surrounding civil service reform legislation. The accord was expected to allow the reform bill to continue to work its way through Congress.
-- JUDGE OVERTURNS INJUNCTION AGAINST CVRD
A judge has overturned an injunction that prevented the government from transfering shares of state mining firm CVRD to its new owners.
-- BANK PROGRAM PROER TO END IN JULY

The controversial program to encourage bank mergers and acquisitions, known as Proer, will end in July, Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola said. Proer, created in October 1995 to strengthen a then weak banking system, has made 20.8 billion reais in credit available to banks.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- SOCCER CORRUPTION COULD LEAD TO INVESTIGATION
Brazil's Attorney General could open up an investigation into alleged corrupt practices by soccer officials.
-- GREMIO DEFEATS CORINTHIANS IN BRASIL CUP
Corinthians lost to Gremio 2-1 in the first semifinal game of the Brasil Cup.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- John Miller, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-248-5414))
